Subject: General

Topic 3.2: Writing practice
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing practice, part of Writing 3.1 Letter formation (8 Lessons) By the end of the sub strand the learne in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: Which items do we use to write, colour and paint letters of the alphabet? 2. Why do we learn letters of the alphabet?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing practice together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and imagination: originality as the learner draws and colours pictures of things found in school.

● Digital literacy: interacting with digital technology as the learner writes letters of the alphabet using digital devices.

Values:
● Responsibility is developed as the learner writes letters of the alphabet independently in sand traces, slate boards, books and

any other writing tools.

● Unity is enhanced where the learner practises writing letters of the alphabet using ICT letter writing games in groups.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Self-discipline is enhanced as the learner learns to work collaboratively with others and without unnecessary conflicts.

Link to other Learning Areas: Creative Activities as learner joins dots, traces letters and colours them.

Suggested learning resources: Sand traces, slate boards, books and any other writing tools, digital device, pictures, plasticine

clay, dough, colour pencils, chart, letter cards
